title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 6
paragraphs: Among the rest of the Thracians, the custom is to sell their children to be taken away out of the country. They do not keep watch over their maidens, but allow them to have intercourse with whatever men they please; but over their wives they keep very strict watch, and they buy their wives for great sums of money from the parents. To be tattooed is considered a mark of noble birth, and to be unmarked is a sign of low birth. Not to work is counted most honorable, and to be a tiller of the soil is above all else dishonorable. To live by war and plunder is the most honorable thing of all.
